title: Comfort, Mobility & Daily Care
html:
Basic care supports comfort, function, dignity, and prevention of secondary harm. The RN individualizes assistance instead of doing everything for the client or assuming independence.

Protect function

  • Encourage the safest level of participation in hygiene, mobility, eating, and elimination.
  • Use positioning and assistive equipment to reduce falls, pressure, aspiration, and injury.
  • Balance activity with rest, then reassess tolerance.
Before oral intake
When swallowing safety is uncertain, pause intake and assess according to the care plan and facility process. Upright positioning reduces risk but does not replace evaluation.

Treat pain as multidimensional

Assess location, quality, severity, timing, function, and the client's goals. Combine ordered pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic measures when appropriate, then evaluate both relief and adverse effects.

Prevent pressure injury

Inspect risk areas, manage moisture, support nutrition and mobility, offload pressure, and reposition based on the client's condition and plan. Document skin findings and response rather than only task completion.
